subtopics.title: Growth Against Development — Two Different Questions

questions.question: Economic growth is measured as ...
options: the annual percentage change in real GDP
the annual change in nominal GDP, inflation included
the rise in the Human Development Index
the change in government spending

questions.question: Real GDP grows at 1% while the population grows at 1.5%. What is happening to the average person?
options: They are getting richer, because GDP is growing
They are getting poorer, because output per person is falling
Nothing — population growth does not affect income per person
It cannot be determined from these figures

questions.question: The three dimensions of the Human Development Index are ...
options: exports, imports and the exchange rate
inflation, unemployment and growth
a long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living
savings, investment and consumption

questions.question: An economy expanding on capital-intensive mineral exports while employment and schooling stand still illustrates ...
options: development without growth
balanced growth and development
a recession
growth without development — the enclave pattern

questions.question: Which are demand-side instruments for raising growth?
options: Expansionary fiscal policy, lower interest rates, and courting export demand
School reform and port maintenance
Competition policy and deregulation
Skills training and research incentives

questions.question: Why are grants to poorer households considered potent spending fuel?
options: Because they are the largest budget item
Because poorer households spend a high fraction of every extra rand, powering the multiplier
Because they replace all other policies
Because they are financed by exports

questions.question: The 'import wall' weakens South African demand stimulus because ...
options: imports are banned during stimulus
exports rise faster than imports
a high marginal propensity to import lets much of the stimulus leak abroad
the exchange rate is fixed

questions.question: "Demand cannot conjure the electrician who was never trained" expresses which wall?
options: The inflation wall
The debt wall
The import wall
The structure wall — supply-side constraints that spending cannot remove

questions.question: Supply-side approaches aim to ...
options: expand the economy's capacity to produce, shifting the production possibility frontier outward
increase consumer spending this quarter
raise the general price level
reduce exports to protect home supply

questions.question: Why does failing infrastructure 'tax the entire economy simultaneously'?
options: Because the state raises taxes to repair it
Because unreliable power, ports and rail raise every producer's costs at once
Because it only affects exporters
Because infrastructure is not part of supply

questions.question: A fair criticism of supply-side measures is that they ...
options: work too quickly to be measured
have no effect on long-run growth
are slow, can be regressive in the short run, and depend on state capacity to deliver
always cause inflation

questions.question: The mature evaluation of demand-side against supply-side approaches is ...
options: choose demand-side only, because it is fast
choose supply-side only, because it is durable
choose neither and let markets decide
sequencing and proportion — demand carries the present while supply builds the future

subtopics.title: South Africa's Endeavours and the North-South Divide

questions.question: Which sequence lists South Africa's post-1994 strategies in the correct order?
options: RDP, GEAR, ASGISA, NDP
GEAR, RDP, NDP, ASGISA
NDP, ASGISA, GEAR, RDP
ASGISA, NDP, RDP, GEAR

questions.question: The honest two-handed verdict on South Africa's record is ...
options: total failure on every front
macro stability and a real social wage achieved, while growth trailed population and the named constraints remain
complete success of every plan
growth exceeded every target but development lagged

questions.question: Which mechanism helps hold the north-south gap open?
options: Remittances flowing from north to south
South-south trade agreements
Tariff structures taxing processed goods more heavily than raw ones, discouraging southern factories
The rise of China, India and Brazil

questions.question: South Africa 'straddles the line' between north and south because ...
options: it lies on the equator
its economy is entirely agricultural
it belongs to no international organisations
it combines northern-grade finance, universities and industry with southern-grade unemployment, inequality and poverty

subtopics.title: The Payslip and the Report Card

questions.question: In the two-households story, the payslip stands for ...
options: economic growth — the rand total of what gets produced and earned
economic development — the quality of life
the Human Development Index
government spending

questions.question: "A payslip growing slower than the family is a pay cut wearing a party hat" warns us to ...
options: ignore inflation when measuring growth
divide real growth by population before celebrating it
count nominal GDP only
measure growth in US dollars

questions.question: The second household — flat income but children schooled, medicine collected, home secured — shows that ...
options: growth always brings development
development is impossible without growth
development indicators can improve even while income stands still
report cards depend only on payslips

questions.question: The honest one-sentence summary of South Africa's recent record is ...
options: strong growth and weak development
strong growth and strong development
no growth and no development
a payslip barely keeping pace with the population, and a report card better than the payslip explains

subtopics.title: Feed the Fire or Build the Stove

questions.question: In the kitchen story, feeding the fire represents ...
options: demand-side policy — putting spending money into pockets so the multiplier spreads warmth
supply-side policy — building productive capacity
monetary tightening
trade protection

questions.question: "Pour money in when the pots are already full and you get higher prices, not more food" describes ...
options: the import leak
the inflation limit of demand stimulus when supply is the real constraint
the debt burden
the multiplier effect

questions.question: Which items belong to building the stove?
options: Bigger grants and lower interest rates
More advertising and higher prices
Wiring the house, fixing the bakkie, finishing school and college, making the street safe for a shop
Borrowing for this month's groceries

questions.question: The 'two clocks' conclusion says ...
options: the fire and the stove answer the same question
the stove should always come first
the fire should always come first
the fire feeds this winter while the stove serves all winters — so run both in proportion

questions.question: In the world-scale story, the suburb's children mainly inherit ...
options: working systems — schools that teach, courts that decide, grids that hold
cash savings only
mineral deposits
trade tariffs

questions.question: The 'curious tariff at the suburb's gate' — raw goods nearly free, manufactured goods taxed — discourages ...
options: the suburb's own farming
southern industrialisation, keeping the street selling raw materials
all international trade
emigration from the street

questions.question: Which developments are redrawing the north-south map?
options: Falling world trade and closed borders
The end of all migration
East Asian industrialisation, south-south trade, the AfCFTA, and remittances rivalling aid
The abolition of debt everywhere

questions.question: South Africa as 'the corner house' means every big essay should ...
options: treat South Africa as purely northern
treat South Africa as purely southern
avoid mentioning South Africa
hold both questions at once — growth to afford the future, development so everyone arrives there
